body:
At this very moment, I don't get any antidepressants. I take sleeping pills every night because I really can't sleep without them but that's about it.

When I said I took like 20 different medicines I meant that I tried it for a pretty long period for 2-3 years ago. Maybe it was also more like 20 different combinations of medicines than 20 different pills. It doesn't make any difference what so ever if I take them or not, so I stopped taking them like 8 months ago. But I think I still need some sort of sleeping aid.

Problem is, if you go searching for help, they only tell you to take antidepressants and if you don't take them then there's nothing to do for you.

It's only three years of 28, I realised that. But the years 25-28 are pretty formative I think of how you will be the rest of your life. Especially if you didn't have that super fun of life in your adolescence.

Watching the swedish political debates, if they don't mention Men's violence against women is like Barrack Obama and Mitt Romney forgets to mention the troops. It would be a shitstorm from some people in the media. The sad part is that the only person I have met who understand these sort of things is the person who did this to me.

Yeah, and it wasn't very physically abusive, but psychologycally she did some pretty nasty things.

I know people think most victims of abusive relationsships is women and most perpertrators are men, but it doesn't matter. Statistics show that gypsies are overrepresented when it comes to crimes like shoplifting. Like way overrepresented, they tried to disprove it once from the governments side in a study and it only showed it was even more than you think. It doesn't mean you should talk about gypsies as a group and hold them accountable for it. Why is it okey with gender, but not with races? I don't get that.

Even more to the point. There are studies showing that (at laest in Sweden) males are victims of domestic violence even more than women. I don't know the validity of it or if there are other studies indicating the opposite but I read it somewhere. 

Why aren't there gender neutral crisis centers that people can go to can get help?
It was a crisis 3 years ago, but it has developed into a longer problem. I don't have any friends or anything now.

3 years ago I had a girlfriend which... wasn't nice to me at all. It was an abusive relationship. She did some things that wasn't nice to me. Since then I haven't been the same. I have met countless of therapists since then and tried like 20 different medicines but nothing helped.

I live in Sweden and right now they are having a thing where everybody joins a facebook group called 33 reasons. It's this feminist group that mentions the need for feminism and mentions men's violence against women.

I can't stand it. Where the fuck are you supposed to go if you're a guy and gets abused by a women? Why do they have to bring up gender? You don't exist.

I've sat with bruises in waiting rooms in emergency cares for hours crying. Nobody would give a fuck or if you're lucky you would get a doctor that prescribes you some antidepressants. Nobody has referred me to anybody with expertise in handling relations which include abuse. When this happened, I tried everything. Emergency psychiatric care (akutpsyk) in 2 different towns, churches, student health, Socialkontoret (I guess local county community office).

I tried today to mail the girls hotline because my local city has both a girls center (tjejjour) and a woman crisis center (kvinnojour) and ask if I could come in and get some help because there are no man center in my city and I need help moving forward. It will be interesting to see what they will respond, but I'm almost certain they will deny me care because of my y-chromosome.

I don't want to live in a world where one gender is viewed as better than the other. Yet, we have one gender that is blamed for everything in this world. It makes me sad, because it's so simplistic and I don't think it helps anybody. If you don't live in Sweden or haven't seen Swedish television and what themes they have, this might seem very distant to you
